newsitem.title: UK: Avondale says hopes for new tanker orders.
newsitem.headline: Avondale says hopes for new tanker orders.

text.p: Avondale Industries Inc said Thursday it expects new opportunites to win contracts to build commercial oil tankers.
Avondale chairman and chief executive Albert Bossier said: "We expect other opportunities for additional contracts to develop."
The New Orleans-based naval and commercial shipbuilder won a $332m order to build two 125,000 dwt Suezmax crude oil tankers for Atlantic Richfield Co Marine in the second quarter.
Bossier said: "An important strategic objective has been to build a more balanced base of work between commercial and military contracts."
"The $332 million contract award during the second quarter for two crude carriers for ARCO Marine is indicative of Avondale's potential to capitalize on our proven shipbuilding expertise."
Avondale spokesman Eugene Simon said the shipbuilder was in the running for further commercial tanker newbuilding contracts.
"I think it is pretty common shipping industry knowledge that there are a number of parties looking at tanker newbuilding contacts at US yards," said Mr Simon.
Industry sources said that potential new tanker purchasers included British Petroleum in collaboration with Overseas Shipholding Group Inc Group and Sea River Maritime.
Philadelphia-based Maritrans Inc has an order for six US domestic trade handysize products tankers pending with Avondale.
Simon said comfirmation of the order would depend on Maritrans Inc securing newbuilding finance.
Avondale Thursday announced second quarter net income of $6.4 million, compared with $14.3 million a year earlier which included an income tax benefit of $9.0 million.
Second quarter net sales were $145.8 million against $152.6 million a year earlier.
Bossier said the tankers Avondale will build for ARCO Marine will comply with the double-hull standards mandated by the Oil Pollution Act of 1990.
They are both due to be delivered in 2000 and will be employed in the Alaska-US West Coast trade.
Their comparatively high cost is due to a high specification design incorporating duplicate propulsion systems, Avondale said.
